entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Convened via Kenya Gazette Notice No. 380 of 22nd January, 2020)

entries.label: heading
entries.text: The House met at the Senate Chamber, Parliament Buildings, at 2.00 p.m.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: [The Speaker (Hon. Lusaka) in the Chair]

entries.label: heading
entries.text: HEARING AND DETERMINATION OF THE PROPOSED REMOVAL FROM OFFICE, BY IMPEACHMENT, OF THE GOVERNOR OF KIAMBU COUNTY

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Honourable Senators, we had a break and, therefore we are going to continue with our programme. According to our programme, I will now invite the county assembly to give evidence.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let us have the county assembly.

entries.label: heading
entries.text: PRESENTATION OF THE CASE OF THE KIAMBU COUNTY ASSEMBLY

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, before the County Assembly takes the Floor, I had earlier indicated to my learned colleague on the part of the County Assembly that there will be an application that we will be making before they make their case. I will be seeking your leave that I make that application at this stage. You recall that in our opening remarks, we made reference to the fact that we shall be making an application for admission of certain critical evidence outside the prescribed time. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will be seeking your leave to make that application, of course, noting that under rules of procedure No.13, there is proviso for making an application on a preliminary question. The nature of my application will be critical to how this process proceeds. Therefore, I would be urging that you grant me leave to make that application for admission of those documents outside that time that was prescribed at this Senate. If you grant me that leave, I will prosecute that application in very few minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: County Assembly, do you have any objection to that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Mbuthi Gathenji
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we do not have an objection to the leave sought to make the application but we will respond substantively to the application once it is made.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Okay, since the County Assembly has agreed, and this is their case, you may proceed to put the application.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Thank you too, counsel for the County Assembly for the indulgence. This application is founded under the Fifth Schedule of the rules of procedure of determination of the question of the proposed removal of a governor, and specifically Rule No.29, in which any question on admissibility of evidence and any question incidental thereto shall be determined by the Speaker. Mr. Speaker, Sir, in determination of the application that we are making, which is admission of the Governor's response at the witness statements and the documents thereto, we are alive to Standing Order No.12 in which any question or issue that has not otherwise been provided for by the Standing Orders shall be determined on the basis of the Constitution, forms and precedents---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order. What is your point of order, Sen. Orengo?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we had no notice of this application that is being made. We did not have it in our documents. The notice we have in the application raises four issues. Since we are time bound in the work we are doing, if we are going to have preliminary objections one after the other, and suppose each is going to take 30 minutes, if we go by Standing Order No.13, would it not be better for the counsel for the Governor to give indication how many preliminary applications he is going to make? This is because we have only two days to sit, hear them and make a determination. Could he tell us how many applications he wants to make? Then it may be better for those applications to be handled together or be handled in the process of the proceedings. As they argue their case, they can make those applications. Otherwise, we may find we are going to spend the whole day on these preliminary issues without going to the substance and the time they have for each application here. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I note that in the notice that they have filed, they raised four issues but when I had the address, it looks like they have many more issues. We need to have some understanding so that our work is done in an orderly fashion. That is not to say that he does not have the right for a hearing. In fact, I am trying to help if he can---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let him respond first.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'anga Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you very much, honourable Senator. The application we are making: One, I am starting with the admission of the documents and evidence out of time. That is the first application. The second one is whether the preliminary questions that we fashioned and filed before this Senate should be argued before a merit consideration of the impeachment proceedings. Third will be a request to summon certain key witnesses. I will cite the relevant provisions that enable this Senate and the Speaker to summon relevant witnesses who may be having evidence material to the questions that are before this Senate. What I wish to point out is that I noticed Rule 13 provides for 30 minutes. For this Senate's comfort, I will not take the 30 minutes. I can consolidate those three questions so that my learned friend has a chance to respond to the three and then a determination can be made.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Proceed, Sen. Mutula Kilonzo Jnr.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, my good learned friend ought to make an election. In his preliminary objection that he has filed, in Ground No. 3, he wants this disposed off first before any other matter. He, therefore, has to be absolutely clear about what he wants to do first. This is because it presupposes that he wants this issue determined first, and, therefore, the other ones will follow by virtue of the decision that will be made by this House on this preliminary objection that is already on record. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Yes, Sen. Wetangula.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, my two distinguished learned friends are absolutely right. The learned friend representing the Governor should elect. He has filed a preliminary objection which, if he succeeds, the proceedings will end. Therefore, the issue of adducing evidence out of time will not arise. He should choose whether to prosecute this application that is on record; that will have far-reaching consequences on the proceedings depending on what we rule. Thereafter, he can seek leave to bring additional evidence. Otherwise, it can be construed that in seeking to bring additional evidence, he is abandoning the objection that is on record; that is saying that, they are improperly before this House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Okay. Sen. Murkomen, proceed before he responds.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I totally agree with the interventions of my learned colleagues. The only thing is that the Standing Orders make it clear that any preliminary objection should only take 30 minutes. For our comfort, it is good that he has given us notice that he will take only 30 minutes for all the three preliminary objections, if the House allows. Maybe the question that Sen. Wetangula is asking is the sequencing. Should we first hear the one that is in the file? However, bearing in mind that even when he reverts back to making a case on the other objections, in this case he should not exhaust his 30 minutes. This is because the Standing Orders say that for all the preliminary objections, we are going to use 30 minutes. That is my interpretation of the relevant Standing Order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Can you respond?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. The reason why we have started with the admission of documents is because our preliminary objection is largely based on evidence which is in those documents. For instance, there is an issue as to the threshold - whether the minimum number of Members of County Assembly (MCAs) that are supposed to vote and validly pass a resolution to impeach - were present. We have logs which were not attached by the County Assembly showing the MCAs that were present at the Assembly. I appreciate the comments by my learned colleagues - the Senators - that yes, the preliminary objection is purely on a point of law, but on undisputed evidence. Now, that evidence apparently is not before this Senate by the County Assembly; but it is evidence that we are seeking for admission before this assembly. Mr. Speaker, Sir, whereas we can urge the preliminary questions first, it is important that such critical evidence is also placed properly before this Senate. That is why I set out that sequence. Therefore, if you allow, I can urge for the admissibility of documents out of time for three preliminary questions, then, of course, the preliminary question on whether the preliminary objective should be heard first or in what sequence should it be heard? Third, the request I had mentioned about summoning certain persons who are critical in the fair determination of this impeachment question. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: What you do is you use the 30 minutes to plead for all the three that you have put forward, and then we will make a ruling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I appreciate, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Yes, Sen. Orengo.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Orengo spoke off record)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the point which has been made is the point made by Sen. Wetangula. My understanding of the preliminary objection which has been filed is that there are no proper proceedings before us. We do not have jurisdiction. Now, to urge that position; to call in evidence now would mean that we go into a hearing, and that is what we are trying to avoid so that we deal with the question of the preliminary objection. However, if he wants additional evidence, then I think it will be neater for us to go into the hearing. Allow the County Assembly to bring their evidence, and when it comes to the time for the governor to plead his case, then at that time he can make an application that, "I need additional evidence." That is the way it should be done. However, if he is doing it this way, then it means that he is going against the application. The notice of preliminary objection should then be withdrawn, and then he can go on with that application. But if he got the point of Sen. Wetangula, I think it is helping his case. I would want to listen very carefully to what Sen. Wetangula said, which is that either there are proper proceedings before us, or there are no proceedings. He should, therefore, persuade us that there are no proper proceedings before us. When he is doing that, you do it on the basis of what is on record, which we have already.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Counsel, you have heard what Sen. Orengo has said. Do you want to respond or should I make a ruling?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I heard you make a determination that within the 30 minutes, I deal with the three preliminary questions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Order! The Senate is a court, and you have heard what they have also said and the issues they have raised. So, the choice is yours to either follow what Sen. Orengo has told you or I make a ruling on how we proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I can respond to Sen. Orengo's comments. First, we appreciate that there is a preliminary objection that we filed on the law. It will still require your determination as to the order of precedence; whether we should start with that preliminary objection first. It is the case of the Governor that because it touches on the foundation of this impeachment proceedings, that it be heard first. Having said that, Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have also raised a critical issue; that that argument will be based on material that is not before the Senate which we are seeking the leave of this Senate and the Speaker to admit out of time. So, they are conjoined twins because if we then do not admit the documents as we prosecute the preliminary objection, what shall we be referring to? That is the nature of the request.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.text: Order, Senators. Listening to both sides, you all want to be heard. I think this Senate is there to hear and be fair to all of you. So, I will apply Rule No. 29 which states that: "Where on a particular question or matter, including but not limited to questions of evidence, materiality, relevance, competency or admissibility of evidence and any question consequential or incidental thereto, no provision has been made in the Standing Orders or in this Rules, the Speaker of the Senate shall rule on the question or matter and the ruling of the Speaker shall be final. Therefore, my ruling is that since all of you want to be heard, the county assembly will give their evidence and when your time comes, you will make the request on whether you want more documents to be admitted or not. So, proceed, county assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I believe that the witness needs to be sworn.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The witness for Kiambu County Assembly, Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui, took the oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Hon. Kinuthia, please give the Senate your full name and designation.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: My name is Solomon Kinuthia Wambui. I am an elected Member of County Assembly (MCA) for Ndumberi Ward. I also moved the proposed Motion for Impeachment of Gov. Waititu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Hon. Kinuthia, have you sworn a witness statement in support of the proceedings here?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I swore a witness statement on 25th January, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Is that the document that appears in the bundle that was submitted by the county assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Murkomen? Let us minimize the points of order so that we can proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am sorry to interrupt. I am doing this on behalf of many of our Members on this side who have asked the same. I want us to be clear. It has nothing to do with the witness who is making a presentation. We need clarity on whether your earlier ruling is in effect that the question as to the issues on the preliminary objection - as to whether there was an impeachment that took place in the county assembly or not. Is it in your ruling that it has been postponed to be determined? Will we have a question at the end that this House will make a determination on the question of whether an impeachment happened in Kiambu or not, or we are left to make a determination on the charges at the far end? That is the confusing issue about your ruling. In other words, it means that you have dispensed the preliminary objection which means that he can only use it as point of argument on the charges before us. However, the House will never have the opportunity to make a determination as to whether the issue of an impeachment having taken place in the county assembly happened or not. Will the Speaker dispense of such a serious and weighty matter without an opportunity for the House to vote in future?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: The House will have an opportunity because a Motion will be brought. We will also go in Camera where all the information and issues that have been provided will be raised at that particular point. As you vote, you will be voting with the issues raised in mind. So, you will have an opportunity to interrogate all those things as part of the evidence. This is because some of the issues raised, for example, on whether there was no quorum or not are part of the evidence that will be given and will be looked at when we retreat into camera and make a determination. That is my ruling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Murkomen, you are eating into the time of the House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is extremely important that when the House makes a decision at the end, there is a question on whether an impeachment took place in Kiambu County. I am asking you this because with your ruling, what is left for us is to canvass and deal with the charges. The question that will obviously be dealt with by this House tomorrow is on voting on charge one, two, three and four. My question is, will this House have an opportunity to first of all, vote on whether an impeachment took place or not? If the governor is guilty of the charges, which I am not saying he is because it depends on evidence and so forth, there still will be a substantive question on whether or not an impeachment took place in the County Assembly of Kiambu. That would have a major implication on the decision that you make on the four charges. We do not want to confuse that because we raised the caution earlier. If this process will be subjected to further testing out there, we want the country to know what the Senate decides on the procedure of the County Assembly of Kiambu, either a fair hearing or substantively, whether there was a proper voting on impeaching of the governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: That is the exact evidence that we are listening to now. So, let us listen to the evidence which will determine whether an impeachment took place or not. You have an opportunity---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I want the Senate Majority Leader to listen to me a little bit. I find myself in an odd situation because we should not be participating at this time. We also want to make sure that there is fair hearing which is important. The county assembly has put up a case not just of the charges. They have also given us a record of what happened at the County Assembly of Kiambu, who was there and who was not. So, the question as to whether or not there was an impeachment is important throughout from the moment we start to listen and determine this issue. The county assembly has filed its papers in support of the fact that there was an impeachment. The governor, in his defence, has said that there was no impeachment and for that purpose he has raised a preliminary objection to say that there was no impeachment. So, during the hearing, that is a question that we have to deal with when we are asked to respond and vote.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order Members. I made a ruling. In my understanding the counsel has said that he will need to produce more evidence to support the objection. So, let us proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui, I asked you a question on whether you had made a witness statement. I want you to identify that witness statement in the bundle. I am referring to the fourth witness statement in the bundle. Please confirm that it is your statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I confirm that I made that statement on 25th January, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, unfortunately, the paginating of the bundle starts after the statements. There are four statements which end at the beginning of page one. I would like hon. Kinuthia to give the Senate a brief of his qualifications and his role within the County Assembly of Kiambu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am a Certified Public Accountant (CPA), a Certified Public Secretary (CPS) and a member in good standing of the Institute of Certified Public Accountant (Kenya) - ICPAK and the Kenya Institute of Management (KIM). I am an Alumnus of the University of Nairobi where I graduated with a Master's Degree in Finance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Kinuthia indicated that he was the Mover of the Motion in the County Assembly of Kiambu. I would like him to briefly take us through the process that he went through in moving that Motion and direct us to where it is in his witness statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I filed the Motion for the removal of the Governor of Kiambu County, hon. Ferdinand Ndung'u Waititu, on 3rd December, 2019. I moved the same Motion on the Floor of the Assembly on 19th December, 2019 and it was successful. The resolution of the Kiambu County Assembly was communicated to the Senate and that is why we are here today to dispense this matter as per the law of the land.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like you to take us through the allegations that you raised in your statement starting with the first allegation on gross violation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. What is it that you allege the Governor did and what evidence you have in support of that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the governor grossly violated the Constitution, the County Governments Act, 2012, the Public Finance Management Act, 2012 and the Public Procurement and Disposal Act. There was lack of accountability in the management of the public finances because the Governor led the Executive in incurring unsustainable pending bills in terms of commitment to contractors. The Governor went over and above the budget by issuing award letters and contracts for the tarmacking of roads well above the set budget of Kshs1.1 billion under the approved gazetted budget of the 2018/2019 Financial Year. That omission could not have escaped the knowledge of the Governor granted that he had County Executive Committee (CEC) members and all the chief officers in charge of the tendering process report directly to him. An over commitment of 200 per cent could not have escaped the attention of the Governor. It was safe to presume that it was officially sanctioned by the Office of the County Governor. The contractors were duped into responding to advertisement for tenders and award letters which there was no intention whatsoever to honour them other than gain personal benefit though the mode of kickbacks.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like us to drill down to the various allegations. You mentioned that there is a huge pending bill according to Paragraph 13. I would like you to look at the document that starts at Page Three and identify the document attached.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the document is an annexure of the Auditor-General's audited financial statement for the County Executive of Kiambu for the year ending June 2018. The purpose of the annexure is to give a brief of the status of the pending bills of the Kiambu County Government at the time the Governor took office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, can hon. Kinuthia give us a summary of the table on Page 21 of the document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the table on Page 21 gives a breakdown of the pending accounts payable, the pending staff payables and other payables as per the audited position of the 2018/2019 Financial Year. You realize that for most of that year, the former Governor was still in office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Kinuthia, is your allegation of Kshs2.3 billion in pending bills backed by the Auditor-General's report?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, sure.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like hon. Kinuthia to give us a summary of his second allegation listed on paragraph 14.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the approved and gazetted development budget for roads, transport, public works and utilities for the 2018/2019 Financial Year is indicated on the third row from the bottom in the table on Page 34.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, is that the budget figure based on audited figures?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is the gazetted budget which has been passed and signed by the Governor himself.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Kinuthia, how does your allegation in paragraph 15 relating to the budget that has been passed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are making a statement of fact that the county executive arm of government made commitments in respect for various road tarmacking tender worth, Kshs3.3 billion whereas it was fully aware that the only money available to cater for the contract was only Kshs1.1 billion thereby committing the county over and above budget to 200 per cent of the approved budget.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Kinuthia, where is the evidence of the awards of tenders worth Kshs3.3 billion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the evidence is in pages 35 to 49. The evidence is proof that the advertisement of the tenders was done in newspapers of national circulation and that we appointed county tender valuation committees to vet these tenders when aware that we did not have a budget for the same.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, since hon. Kinuthia, represents the county assembly in these proceedings, will you invite the procurement officer to confirm the documentation that you have alluded to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Director Procurement will appear before the House confirm the above statements of facts.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like hon. Kinuthia to highlight his allegation against the Governor according to Paragraph 21. What is your allegation against the Governor there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as a man of the world and a person who has lived in this country for over 30 years, I am well aware that the only motivation that the Governor would have had to over- commit the county to the tune of Kshs3.3 billion was only to collect 10 per cent kickback from such award.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: I would like you to go to paragraph 29 of your statement. Please, tell us what that relates to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: This is a breakdown of various companies which were registered between October 2017 and March 2019. The wife and daughters of the Governor who is taking the stand today participated in the award of tenders from Kiambu County Government without actually declaring interest and they were paid expeditiously for services they provided.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: In terms of the documentation to support the award letters, contracts and CR 12 to back up this, did you provide this?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: This is the information that was attached to the resolution that came to the Senate on 23rd December. The CR 12s are attached as well as the payment vouchers, which show a time of between 60 to 90 days between the date of registration and the date that the payment vouchers were generated to pay listed companies in this list.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: If we can move on to paragraph 30 of your Witness Statement, tell us what the allegation was before the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It was the consensus of the County Assembly that hon. Waititu was in full knowledge that his next of kin in terms of daughters and wife were trading with the county. He never disclosed conflict of interest and neither did he prevent them from trading with the county, contrary to the stated rules, especially on the Public Procurement and Disposal Act, 2015. So, that shows the collusion and conspiracy to benefit from an office held by the Governor. Hence, it was consensus of the Assembly that that is impeachable conduct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Moving away from the procurement questions, if we can go to paragraph 26 of your Witness Statement on Crimes under the National Law, what was the allegation and what was the evidence that was presented by yourself in respect of that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Kindly come up again.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: If you go to paragraph 26, under that, there is Crimes under the National Law which proceeds to the next page. Please tell us what that allegation was and what evidence you presented.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Under paragraph 26, the issue was failure by the Governor to establish a County Budget and Economic Forum, which was intentional and calculated to ensure that the citizens do not participate in county matters. Moving on to the other paragraph below, which is Crimes under the National Law, it is about violation of Article 40 of the Constitution and Section 155 of the Land Act, 2012, by unlawful acquiring and occupying property in Thika Town owned previously by Ms. Cecilia Njoki Mbugua.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: In respect of that allegation, do you have a witness who will come and table the reports of the Commission on Administrative Justice (CAJ) as well as the various transfers that related to that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Mbuthi Gathenji
entries.text: Coming to the allegation in respect of employment, there were certain allegations you made about how the Governor conducted himself in regard to employment. What was the allegation there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The allegation was that he disregarded the County Public Service Board (CPSB) as an organ created by the County Governments Act, 2012. That is Section 74. He usurped the responsibility of interviewing and hiring county workers without the backing of the law.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Do you have a witness who has set out what that procedure is?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, we do have a witness who has voluntarily rendered a witness statement to that effect.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Is that the statement of Mr. Martin Njoroge?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: If I may take you to the pages 125 through to 127 and also pages 128 through to 138, please tell us the difference between those two bundles.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The first bundle from pages 125 through to 128 is attached for purposes of contrasting. Ideally, the hiring process should come after an advertisement by the CPSB. Then it should be followed by a sitting. On page 125, you can see they referred to a memo referred to as CPSB/ST/7/ii/VOL.IV/49/MW dated 3rd April, 2019, where a post of Chief Driver, Job Group "H" was advertised. The terms of service and the pay grades are itemized and signed below by the County Secretary. Ideally that is what should happen. There should be a sitting by the CPSB and a resolution and then a memo communicated to the CPSB, so that the hiring process is effected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: What about the letters on pages 128 to 137?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: What is on pages 128 through to 137 shows the prevailing situation in Kiambu where the Governor designs a vacancy and conducts hiring himself in complete disregard of the CPSB. Ultimately he signs the letter and directs various officers in the Payroll Office and the County Secretary's Office who is the Head of Public Service to recognise that hiring decision.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: When you look at those letters, if I can just refer to one or two of them, do you know the fate of these people who were hired by the Governor directly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Upon a random inquiry by the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) about hiring decisions, they were fired via a memo drafted by the County Secretary. Instructions were given to the Director of Human Resource (DHR) to stop their salaries. Those who were affected were 26 in number. The same fate befell the casual workers who were hired without proper regard to the labour procedures.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Hon. Solomon, were you present during the impeachment proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I was.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Can you tell the House how the proceedings proceeded?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The proceedings were robust as you would expect of such a Motion which is important to the county. The MCAs both in support and in complete opposition to the Motion were present. There was a group that chose to retreat away from the Assembly's premises. All the same, we proceeded under the guidance of the administrative wing of the Assembly which is led by the Clerk and the Speaker. We voted towards 6 o'clock in the evening. The side that was amenable to the impeachment of Gov. Waititu carried the day.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Now, if I can refer you to the Standing Orders of the County Assembly of Kiambu, can you confirm to the House what method of voting was utilised at the impeachment? I can see that you have electronic voting, voting by acclamation, roll call voting--- What was the method that was utilised for voting?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We used roll call voting, where each side of the divide had an appointed teller by way of consensus, and we also had clerks assisting in terms of tallying.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Now, if you may look at your Standing Order No.97, is that the one that governs the procedure for roll call voting?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: If you look at Standing Order No.98, which makes provision for correction of errors during the roll calling voting itself, was there any time that the governor or any member raised an issue as to confusion or error in the roll call voting, under the said Standing Order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: No, I do not recall any member raising concern about confusion or errors.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: You are still a Member of the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Now, after the voting had been done and the resolution sent, are you aware whether anyone has invoked Standing Order No.99 asking that whatever it is that had been determined by the roll call should be corrected in the manner provided for under that Standing Order No.99?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I am not aware of efforts within the assembly emanating from Standing Order No.99.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: That would be all for this witness, and he is available for cross-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you very much, Hon. Speaker and hon. Senators. I will begin the cross-examination of this witness and then yield the Floor to my learned colleagues.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am sorry. With your indulgence, I have just one more question. Do you wish to produce your witness statement and the documents that you have produced here to the House?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Kinuthia, I want us to start with what exactly transpired on the Floor of the Assembly on the 19th of December. First, can you confirm that the totality of the Members of the County Assembly of Kiambu is 92?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, it is public knowledge.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Kindly just answer the question the way I have asked; whether it is public knowledge or otherwise is not the question. Can you confirm, Mr. Solomon, that out of the 92 members, 30 members were not present in the assembly on the 19th of December?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I am not aware of the abstentions and the attendance of members. Administrative support is provided by the Clerk's office and I chose to adopt the position taken by the clerk and the speaker.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Were you present on the Floor of the assembly on the 19th?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I was present.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: The question is: Are you aware? If you are not, that is fine. Kindly do not give us stories. Are you aware that actually 35 members were not present on the Floor of the assembly on the 19th? If, no, it is okay; we will proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: No, I am unaware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You are aware that one of the issues the governor is raising is the threshold and that the assembly was served with a preliminary objection saying that the minimum threshold of MCAs were absent on the 19th. Was the assembly served by the Clerk of the Senate with that preliminary objection?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I have come to learn of that letter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua: S
entries.text: o, they were served. So, you knew that there will be a question or issue of numbers that would be up for determination by this Senate. Did you not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is debatable, the Senate ---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, answer my question. Was the assembly aware that there would be a question of numbers that this Senate would be called upon to determine in these proceedings? Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is part of what we are here to determine.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I think it is important that this witness does not prevaricate. I am asking a very direct question. I am asking the question whether the assembly was aware that the question of numbers or threshold of the MCAs that were present on the 19th would be a question for determination by the Senators; yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We received a copy of your preliminary objection---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You did receive; thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: When you looked at the preliminary objection, you noticed that the governor was contesting the actual number that was present and voted on the 19th of December. Did you not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I did go through.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Now, when you notice that, can you just look at the document you have produced before this Senate. Number one, shows, if at all, the actual attendance of MCAs on the 19th of December when the vote is said to have been taken. Do you have any such evidence? Yes or no. That is a document that was prepared by the assembly, hon. Solomon. Just so that we move faster; it is either you have it or you do not? Do you have an attendance list of the MCAs who attended on the 19th?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I do not have it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You do not have it. Do you have a good answer why you do not have it or you were seeking to suppress evidence from the Senate as to the actual number of people that were present on the 19th?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: My work was to move the motion and lobby members to support it, which I did successfully. The rest are statutory laws and each party; the Senate and the speaker of the assembly - everybody has his role, and it is not in my purview to keep records for the assembly. If it was, I would have brought the records here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is okay. We will move on. We know that it is not your work to keep records. So, we will take it that the evidence is just your oral evidence, yet you knew that, that would be a question that was in issue. Is this evidence or material present before the assembly either at the clerk's office or any other office to the assembly--- Is the information regarding the records of those who voted and those that were absent available at the assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The County Assembly of Kiambu is a public institution.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Excuse me, Mr. Solomon. We know it is a public institution. My question is very direct and specific. Is this evidence as to those who voted available at the County Assembly of Kiambu? Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: All information at the assembly is public, and you can make a specific request to the assembly to grant you that information.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Solomon! You will assist this House by answering questions directly the way you are asked. Do not take us into a lot of circumlocutions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Thank you. Much obliged, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, the question is this; and I put it to you, Mr. Solomon: You are the mover of the motion and had a direct interest in the motion. The governor is contesting the threshold. I am asking you: is information or evidence regarding who attended, who voted 'nay' and who voted 'yes' available at the County Assembly of Kiambu? Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But that evidence, you confirm while in oath, is not before this honourable Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I am the one on oath and I am not aware of what the Speaker sent here to the Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I have asked you the questioned and will pose it again. As you testify, you can confirm that this is not evidence that is before this Senate. Yes or no. Is it evidence before this Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I would assume no, because ----

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do not assume, the answer is no; there is no such evidence. Are you aware that under Section 33 of the County Governments Act, for a valid resolution to be passed to impeach a governor, a minimum of two thirds of the membership of the assembly has to vote 'yes' for that resolution?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But we do not have evidence of whether that two-thirds was actually met. Before this Senate this afternoon, that evidence is lacking. Yes or no, Solomon? It is not about thinking because we need to move a bit faster, so that we can save on time. That evidence is not before this Senate. Is it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: If you say so.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Not if I say so, it is not there. Thank you. Let us move on, that is as far as now. I want you to look at the documents that you have produced. First of all, are you aware that under the rules of procedure, the assembly cannot rely on any other additional material than the material that was the basis of the allegation before the assembly? Are you aware that you cannot introduce any new material at the Senate, which was not part of the allegations?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We received a correspondence from Senate-- -

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I am asking: are you aware? Let us go sequentially. Are you aware that the assembly cannot produce additional material that was not part of the allegations before the assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, that I am aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I want you to quickly just skim through the documents that you have relied on. Do you have the documents that were served on the Hon. Governor when the notice of the motion at the assembly was given and the documents, if any, that was supplied to the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have them with you? I just want us to compare. Just a very short exercise; we compare what is now before the Senate and what the governor was actually supplied with. I want to just make this exercise very easy for you. I want to start with some of the documents that you have attached. For instance, you have attached documents. Hon. Senators, let us start with page one, which is a letter to the Commission on Administrative Justice (CAJ), the Ombudsman. Was that letter supplied to the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: No, it was not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, the governor is seeing these documents at the Senate for the first time. Correct? Anyway, you have said it was not. Go to page two. Was that evidence supplied to the governor at the assembly level?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I would assume it was.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Not you would assume. Do you have evidence? It is not an assumption, Solomon, this is a very serious House; it is an impeachment court. Is there evidence that the letter on page two was ever served on the governor, or this is the first time it is being tabled before the Senate? It is either you do not know; yes or no, so that we move on. We need to move a bit faster.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The letter was not supplied because---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It was not supplied, thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It came after the notice of motion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Let us move on. The Auditor General's Report on page three all the way to page 33, signed by Auditor General, Edward Ouko. Was that Auditor General's Report supplied to the governor at the assembly level?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The Governor is the one who was being audited.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, as to who was being audited or not, is not the question. Was that document supplied to the Hon. Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: No, we did not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You did not. So, the governor is seeing it for the first time. Mr. Solomon, page 34 is a supposed summary of expenditure. Is there any evidence that the document on pages 34, 35 and 36 was supplied to the governor at the county assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, this one was supplied to the governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: This one was. Do you have evidence of receipt of that document by the Office of the Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is part of the bundle I handed to the Clerk's office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You must have retained a copy, did you not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Evidence of receipt by the governor of that particular document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I have the received notice of motion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I can provide it to the Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But you do not have it with you. Let us go the report of CAJ, from the Ombudsman on page 50. Do have evidence that that report was again, which is what you are relying on to prosecute a charge of a crime committed against national law; evidence that the report from Ombudsman was supplied to the governor during his impeachment at the assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, this one has.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Receipt of that document by the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is in the bundle we gave to the Clerk.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But you do not have it with you here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Now, you have touched some title documents. Hon. Senators, pages 64 to 74 is a certificate of lease for some property, which bears the name, Cecilia Njoki Mbugua. Is there any evidence that, that certificate of lease was served on the governor before he was supposedly impeached by the assembly? Do you have that evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: This came after.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, the governor was seeing this document yesterday when he was supplied with this document by the Clerk of the Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: This came from the public participation that we held at the assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But the public participation, I presume, if any was conducted, was before a vote was taken?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, in the intervening period between---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, there was opportunity for this material to be served on the governor, because public participation precedes the voting?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He was also a part of those who were invited.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: As to whether he was part is not the question; there was opportunity for the assembly to provide material that came up during the public participation. Was there not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, there was.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But you confirm that even after that information came to the attention of the assembly, it was not served on the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It was served through the Senate recently.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Yes, the question is not whether it was served by the Senate recently--- I am concerned about the service before his impeachment at the assembly? It was not. Answer 'yes' or 'no,' we need to move a bit faster, Solomon.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We did our part in discovery of this material and remitted it to the Clerk.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It was not served on the governor, that is the question. Mr. Solomon, these are not questions you need to think about. It is a question of whether you know or you do not, so that we move on.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It was not served between the 3rd and 19th, but it was served---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It was not served between the 3rd and the 19th, when the governor was supposedly impeached by the Assembly. Is it not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, but it was served on the 27th.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you very much. Now, let us just spend a bit of time on the allegations; that is, on the process. Let us go to some very sensationalized--- You have said about pending bills at paragraph 13, that one of the charges, that is, gross violation of the Constitution, Public Finance Management (PFM) Act and Public Procurement and Disposal Act has to do with pending bills. First of all, you are aware that the issue of pending bills is a national issue and is not unique to Kiambu. Is it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We are demonstrating here---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No! No! Answer my question; it is not about demonstrating. Are you aware that this is a national issue that is bedeviling all the counties in this country?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is very unique to Kiambu?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, it is only Kiambu that has pending bills? Is that your evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Arising out of over commitment.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: As to how it arose is not the question. Is it your testimony that only Kiambu has pending bills out of the 47 counties we have in this country?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I am an MCA in Kiambu. I am well aware of matters Kiambu County.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I did not ask you that. Mr. Solomon, can you just answer the question? Mr. Speaker, Sir, let this witness not take this Senate for granted. It is a very important investigative exercise.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: But I think the answer he has given is adequate. He said he is aware of Kiambu, because he belongs to Kiambu County and not any other county. I think he is right to say that he knows only about Kiambu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Out of the Kshs2.3 billion pending bills, do you have a breakdown to show which of these bills may have been incurred during the previous regime? Do you have evidence of, first, a breakdown? You are talking of Kshs2.3 billion. Out of this Kshs2.3 billion, which ones were incurred by the previous regime?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: If you allow an explanation---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No! No! I am asking: Out of this Kshs2.3 billion pending bills, let us see when they were incurred. This is because you are aware that the governor on trial came in after the 2017 elections.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He was sworn in August, 2017.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Yes, he was sworn in. What I am asking is: out of the Kshs 2.3 billion, which part of those bills, if any, were inherited from the previous regime or do you have a breakdown to show when they were actually incurred and by whom? From your documents, just answer whether you have that evidence from your documents then we move on.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We have not provided that breakdown.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You have not provided that. Okay. Are you aware of any provision under the Public Procurement and Assets Disposal Act that treats pending bills as a crime or a violation?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, Section 135.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Just read for us. Do you have it? Is it Section 135 of Public Finance Management (PFM) Act?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes. It prohibits expenditure above set ceilings.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It prohibits expenditure. You have made reference to Section 35 of the PFM Act. Is that correct? Is Section 35 where you have pegged that particular charge because Section 35 is on stages of budgeting?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Counsel, please pay interest. I said Section 135.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, it is not about paying interest. Let us see that Section 135. Section 135 marginal notes are: "County governments to submit county assembly supplementary budget in certain circumstances." My question is on these pending bills; it is not about submissions of estimates and budgets. First of all, what criminalizes pending bills, because that has been treated as a crime under the charges proposed? Which section of the law criminalizes pending bills?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I am aware with the Chief Officer---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Just tell us because you are the mover of the Motion. You drafted the charge sheet and must have read the law. Which violation? Pending bills is what you have treated as a violation. I am interested in which Section of the law that you now rely on to say was violated by the governor because of incurring these bills that you could not even demonstrate when they were incurred? Do you have that, so that we can move on? First, tell us whether you have that section in the charges.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, we are going with Section 135 of the PFM Act.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Section 135 is your basis?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Section 135 from my Statute, because yours could be different, is on submission of supplementary budgets and not what you are refereeing to. Let us move on, Hon. Solomon. You have referred to the approved budget--- Hon. Senators, this is Paragraph 15 of the witness statement. There were award letters for road tarmacking amounting to Kshs3.3 billion. You have made reference from pages 43 to 49. Let us start with page 43. Just confirm, Hon. Solomon, that page 43 is referring to invitation to tender. Is that what your document talks of?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I made reference to 35 through to 49.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Hang on. I am referring to 43. I will go to that document that you are referring to. From page 43 to 49, they are actually invitations to tender and not the actual tender awards or contracts. Is that what you notice from your bundle? Those are invitations to tender.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: When I was---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Excuse me! We need to move a bit faster. On page 43, just tell us whether from your bundle, those are invitations to tender and not the actual tender documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I think the Counsel needs to let the witness answer. He is misrepresenting the testimony that the witness had given. The witness is trying to correct him and he is trying to bulldoze him. He has quoted the wrong pages that were cited in respect of the schedules, and the witness is trying to answer that. If you ask a question, let it be answered.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am referring to specific pages because in cross-examination, I am supposed to ask a direct question. I am referring the witness--- First and foremost, in cross, I am not limited to even what came out in exam- in-chief. This is cross-examination; a question or material relevant to the issue at hand can be raised. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am raising a question touching on - there is an allegation on award of tenders by the governor, and I am referring the witness to a document. So, I will know the nomenclature of that document. Is it a tender, an invitation to tender or what is it? We cannot misrepresent certain facts. It is either an invitation to tender, a tender document or the contract. Mr. Speaker, Sir, my question is premised on the documents that this witness has produced. I believe that question is proper and in order during cross-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Kindly proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you. Therefore, Hon. Solomon, go to page 43, a very quick exercise. Can you confirm that from what is there, that is an invitation to tender?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, this is an invitation to tender.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Therefore, what I would be interested in--- You have referred to that between October 2018 and 2019, the county issued award letter for road tarmacking amounting to Kshs3.3 billion. This is a notification of award of tender. Can you point to us from the documents this notification of award of tender that the County Government issued?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: On pages 35 and 36, there is a summary of---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Therefore, let us go to page 35. Stop there. Hon. Senators, this witness is saying that, that is what constitutes the letters of award of tender. Do you confirm that what we have is a list that has not been signed and, therefore, not authenticated, and we cannot tell its source? That, that is what is being relied on to say that there was award of tenders of Kshs3.3 billion. That, that is what you have and that is what you want this Senate to take as evidence of award of those tenders; a schedule unsigned, unauthenticated, whose sources and origin cannot be established.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The tender numbers are serialized in the official documents of the county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I did not ask you about the tender numbers but in that list, those tenders are not there, and the actual letters of award of those tenders are not there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We provided this information on the Floor of the Assembly and there is no rebuttal from the governor's side.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Excuse me! As to whether there was no rebuttal, that is not the question.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We did not attach it here, because we assumed that the silence is consent.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you. You did not attach. That is fine. We will take that to be your answer. Let us move on. Let us go to page 35. From pages 35 to 49, do you have contracts that were signed between the County Government of Kiambu and these contractors for those tenders?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I would be willing to produce them today.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is not about willing. You knew that you had been invited to supply evidence to this Senate when you received the invitation to appear.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I have the contracts with me. I will be willing to table them.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Where are they? Do you have them in the document that you filed before the Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: They are here in this file.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That will not assist us because you knew that--- Just like we had a challenge in filing our documents, all this time, from the time you gave the notice on 3rd of December, 2019. You gave a notice of impeachment touching on award of tender and knew you had those documents, but decided not to supply those documents. Now, you want this Senate to take that; what you have just done, raising a hand and saying: "Oh yes, here it is, but Hon. Senators, it is not before you." Let us move on. Let us go to paragraph 21 of the witness statement. Now, you have stated that the purpose of the irregular awards of these tenders was not to provide public roads, but intended to enable the governor obtain personal benefits through kickbacks. First, we have not seen evidence of those tenders. What I am interested in is: Hon. Solomon, you stated that, in fact, the purpose was that so that the Governor can get a tithe; you said 10 per cent. Did you not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I gave a range of 10 per cent.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That is fine. Do you have evidence of these kickbacks from these so called contractors that were given these tenders? We need evidence that there was 10 per cent paid to the governor by these contractors. Is that evidence in your documents?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Not at the moment.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is not there. Alright, let us move on. You have fashioned an allegation to do with--- You have raised an issue of procurement because award and tendering is about procurement. Does the governor sit in the tender committee? Is he a member of the tender committee of the County Government?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He has proper representation.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: As to whether he has proper representation is a question of argument. The question is: is he one of the members or persons who sit in the tender committee that awards tenders?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He is not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Does he sit in the evaluation committee?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He is represented.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No. Does he sit as a person, as a governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: No, he does not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: He does not. Does the governor award tenders?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He does from his modus operandi .

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Oh, he does. Modus operandi is a flowery term. Just show us where from the evidence that you have adduced the governor issued a notification of award of tender in his own hand.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Refer to paragraph 29.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I am interested in the evidence. What is the page number?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is paragraph 29 of the witness statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: What is the page?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is on page 7.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Is that a notification of award of tender in the hand of the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: That is the family tree of the governor and the companies that they own.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I did not ask him about the family tree. He is fashioning his own question and answering it. Mr. Solomon, this is a very serious process. I am asking you a question. You said that the governor issues tenders or awards. My question is: from the documents that you have, can you point out one letter of notification of award of tender by the governor to any of the contractors who may have benefitted from the Kshs3.3 billion tender?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: From paragraph 29, I am persuaded to think-- -

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is not about persuasion. I have asked you for evidence, a document. Mr. Solomon, if you are referring to a letter of notification of award of tender, point us to one signed by the governor awarding a contract to whichever contractor. Do you have a single document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I do not have.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You do not have it. Thank you. Let us go to the question of failure to establish the County Budget Economic Forum. Are you aware that there is a County Budget Economic Forum in Kiambu?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: There is not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: There is none. Okay. When did you learn that Kiambu County Government does not have this important forum called the County Budget Economic Forum?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: There was no involvement of the County Budget Economic Forum in budget formulation for two budget cycles. Their names are not gazetted---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: What intervention, if any, did the County Assembly undertake in its oversight capacity? Did you ever summon the governor and if so, when to question him on failure to constitute that forum?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The record will show that we raised this concern.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Show us the record that shows when he was summoned. It should state something like; "this is the question that we are raising and we want you to appear before the Assembly for you tell us the reason you have not established this particular forum?"

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We summoned the County Executive Committee Member (CEC).

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: When did you summon him? Do you have evidence of the summons when you summoned the CEC to answer to that question?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It can be provided.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It can be provided, but you do not have it. Have you ever summoned the governor himself because the person who is standing trial is the governor for failure to establish this forum? Do you have any summon to the governor by the assembly in its own oversight capacity questioning why he has not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The standing orders do not provide for members to summon a governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: They do not provide. So, in a sense you are saying that the only recourse you would have had is impeaching the governor because he has not established this forum? Does it mean that there are no other oversight mechanisms that can be deployed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have canvassed this issue with his officials, but they are adamant. So, we had no option.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Have you ever thought of going to court to get a mandamus order to compel him to constitute this forum because of failure to comply with a statutory obligation? Has the Assembly ever filed a suit to compel the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We filed a full suit---

entries.label: speech
