entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Oh, you did. What are the particulars and when?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: On the supplementary budget in April.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Not the supplementary budget. I am talking of the issue of the County Budget Economic Forum.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The outcome---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I am asking about the question of failure to establish the County Budget Economic Forum. Is there any suit by the assembly to compel the governor? The assembly feels very strongly that this is a serious violation. Was there any attempt by the assembly to file a suit to compel the governor to establish this? Was that ever done? Has that ever been done by the assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We exercised the other option that we had in law, which was to impeach him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, you have never gone to court though that was an option that was available to you. You could have gone to court to compel the governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The totality of these charges was compelling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Let us move on. We will look at the issue of the so called abuse of office. Are you aware that the governor is currently facing criminal prosecution touching on the issue of conflict of interest?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, with a different set of facts---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I will go there. Are you aware that there is actually a pending criminal prosecution touching on the issue of conflict of interest.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I am aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: In the charges, there is also a charge of conflict of interest touching on award of tenders. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: They are different companies and different circumstances.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: As to whether they are different companies; it is touching on the issue of award of tenders.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, it does.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you. Let us go to the so called immediate family members. Do you have any evidence of the relationship between Susan Wangari Ndung'u and the honourable governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes. I am a family friend and---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No. I am asking you if you have evidence. We could also be family friends to the governor. The question is: do you have evidence of this familial relationship between Susan Wangari Ndung'u and the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Going by the principle of holding out---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: She is a common law wife of the governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is not common knowledge. It is not about taking judicial notice. The governor pleaded not guilty.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Counsel, I said common law wife.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Excuse me! You are saying common law wife.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: By habit and repute.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have evidence or somebody who will come and say: "I was there when the governor was paying dowry to this common law wife and, therefore, this is the wife of the governor?" Do you have that evidence before this Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I attended the traditional dowry negotiation---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It was in Dundori.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have that evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I was among the invited guests.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have that evidence before this Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Granted reasonable time, I will produce photos of me when I joined the family for ngurario .

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Mr. Solomon, I am sure you know that a certificate of marriage can actually be issued even in customary marriages. Do you have a certificate of marriage? It is either we do not or we do not. As to who was present or not, that is not evidence before this Senate. You are saying that Susan is related to the governor by virtue of being husband and wife. The question is: Do you have a marriage certificate showing that Susan Wangari Ndung'u, Identity Number this, is the wife of the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I do not, but I retreated to the traditional ngurario ceremony.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you. Let us go to Monica Njeri Ndung'u. There is Monica Njeri Ndung'u and Diana Wangoko; their so called daughters. Do you have any evidence that these persons listed there--- They only appear in a CR12. Mr. Solomon, your evidence is that there is a lady known as Diana Wangoko Ndung'u without 'Mo,' who shares the name Ndung'u with the governor, and that is the only link that you have between the governor and this so called daughter. Is that the only evidence that you have?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: These are the members listed as beneficiaries in the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have that NHIF document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: With the leave of the Chair, we will provide.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Do you have it? You knew that, that would be a material question, because the governor has denied these charges. Do you have evidence that these have been listed as beneficiaries by the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: With the leave of the Chair, we will produce that document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You do not have it. Let us move on. You made reference to the recruitment of casual labourers and said that just because the governor issued a letter, the recruitment was not proper. Is that your evidence, Mr. Kinuthia? Do you have evidence by a member of the County Public Service Board (CPSB) saying that these persons were actually not recruited by the board, and that the governor proceeded to issue appointment letters on his own motion?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, we do have a statement to that effect sworn by the member of the board.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That is okay. Let us go to that statement. Point us to where is says: "As far as these casuals were concerned we, as a board, did not recruit?" Just show us that statement. I will quickly refer you to it, because it is attached in your document. I believe that this is the one on page--- Which page is it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: On page 1 through to pages 2 and 3 of the bundle, by Martin Njoroge Njeri.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Just show us the paragraph from that statement that says that these letters were issued without recruitment by the County Public Service Board. Take us to the paragraph that says: "We, as a board, did not recruit, but the governor, nonetheless, proceeded to issue letters of appointment to these casuals."

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Paragraph 6 and 8 would---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: What does paragraph 6 say? It says that pursuant to Section 59 (2) and Section 74 of the County Governments Act, the board approves appointment. It just says what the board does. My question is a direct averment in that witness statement; that "We, as a board, or, I as a member of the board, am aware that we did not recruit these persons, and that the governor proceeded to issue appointment letters to those persons."

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Section 74 of the County Governments Act together with paragraph 8 of the statement would---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I will read to you paragraph 8 of the statement. "That, I am aware that during the tenure under investigation, a number of appointments were done in compliance with the laid procedure." Is that what paragraph 8 of your statement reads? This witness is actually confirming that the appointments were done in compliance with the laid procedure, unless you are reading a different statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Continue to the other part.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua: "
entries.text: During the debate on the impeachment Motion, I was made aware that a number of appointments within the county were made outside the knowledge and involvement of the board." He says that he was made aware. This is not the board saying that the recruitment was not done in compliance with the law. It is saying that the assembly made him aware. Other than that statement saying that he was allegedly made aware, where is the actual evidence that, that recruitment was not done in compliance with the law? Mr. Kinuthia, this member of the County Public Service Board is saying that he was made aware by the assembly. It is not the board saying that the appointment was irregular. It is actually the assembly alleging. This now puts the ball directly into your court. As the person alleging and bringing to the awareness of this member to this alleged invalid appointment, where is the evidence that these casuals were actually not recruited in line with the law?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: If you go to page 128 of the bundle, there is no reference to any minute of the board or an official memo from the board conveying the decision to appoint such an officer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Does any appointment letter in the hand of the governor have to make reference to the minute of the board?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Section 74---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Excuse me! Are you saying that any appointment letter issued in the hand of the governor must refer to the minutes of the County Public Service Board?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: With the exclusion of provisions printed by the Transition Authority for personal staff. Any other appointment should make reference to a board sitting and reference of the memo conveying the same appointment to the County Secretary for appointment. The governor has no role there whatsoever.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Where is that in the law under the County Governments Act?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Section 74 gives the exclusive mandate for hiring.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Wait a minute. Let us go to Section 74. Are you saying that Section 74 mandates the governor to refer to minutes any time he is issuing an appointment letter? I will quickly look at Section 74 of the County Governments Act.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Section 74, not 174.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua: "
entries.text: The County Public Service Board shall regulate the engagement of persons on contract, volunteer and casual workers, staff of joint ventures and attachment of interns in its public bodies and offices." My question is very direct. It is not how the County Public Service Board conducts its affairs. I have asked you for a provision in law that says that when the governor is issuing a letter of appointment to whoever, he must refer to the minutes of the County Public Service Board that recruited that person.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Counsel, I answered that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I have asked you a question as to which Section, then you can explain, kindly, Mr. Kinuthia.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Section74 gives exclusive mandate to the board save for positions that were mandated by the Transition Authority (TA).

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That is not my question. My question is not on Section 74.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: 123 is an admission of guilt on the part of the governor and the county secretary.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order! Counsel, you will need to manage time, because we are already over one hour, and you have a maximum of four hours for all the other witnesses. Therefore, let us manage time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That is okay. I am almost done. Those are the letters. You could not show us any evidence of any Section of the law violated because of not referring to the minutes. Let us move on, so that I can give the Floor to my learned colleagues. You have made reference to how the voting was actually done. My learned friend asked you whether there was any correction of errors. Mr. Kinuthia, on the floor of the assembly on the 19th, you are aware that the tellers are supposed to be selected on the basis of who are voting 'Yes' and who are voting 'No', correct? There is a teller for 'No' and a teller for 'Yes.'

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Each party should--- It is by consensus of voting.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Yes, by consensus. Who was the representative of the 'Nay' tellers?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Hon. Nyutu Wamwere.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Confirm that Hon. Nyutu Wamwere, who was representing the 'Nay' tellers actually voted 'Yes.'

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He voted 'Yes.'

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Can you confirm that the only 'Yes' teller, who is Hon. Ikonya from Kiambu town--- Hon. Ikonya, who was initially representing the 'Nay' tellers was actually ejected from the assembly chamber by the Speaker during the voting.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: He was disorderly. He defied the Speaker.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua: H
entries.text: e was actually ejected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The Speaker had no recourse but to eject him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: The one who represented the 'Nay' teller was actually not representing the "Nay" side, but actually representing the 'Yes' voters?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Hon. Nyutu Wamwere was a 'Nay' person, but he had a moment---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, he voted 'Yes', but was allegedly representing the 'Nay' teller.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Voting was on conscience. If his conscience pricked him and he voted 'Yes', we cannot reprimand him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You have made reference to intervention by the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) that led to the firing of these casuals. Do you have these letters from the EACC directing the governor or raising an issue as to the recruitment of these casuals, and that supposedly now led to the hiring of these casuals by the governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: 17th June was all---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, I am asking you if you have that letter from the EACC?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I do not, but---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text:
No, you do not. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will yield the Floor for my learned colleagues to take up further questions in cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Mr. Charles Njenga:

Mheshimiwa,

I only have one question and then we shall rest. On the day of moving of the Motion on 19th December, are you able to confirm that the Governor was represented by two advocates who indicated by way of a letter that they were attending on his behalf the Assembly proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, the Speaker acknowledged their presence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: You were there in the course of proceedings. Is it not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I was.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Is there a moment or an instance when the Speaker gave them a chance to represent the Governor, make representations, answer to the evidence and make submissions in support of the Governor's case? Did he invite them?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The Speaker---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Did he invite them in the course of the proceedings at any one incidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: In the communication from the Chair, the Speaker indicated that they were there to watch brief for the Governor and not to make representations. This is because our Standing Orders are a bit constrained and we do not admit anybody in the plenary other than the Senator and the Governor. Therefore, we were a bit constrained and they were only able to watch brief for the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Therefore, in the impeachment proceedings for the Governor, we are also not Senators and we are in the Senate. We have been invited to speak to the Governor's case. In the Assembly, you confirmed that the Speaker refused despite notice to invite the Governor's advocate to defend him on the Floor and answer to the allegations and to the motion and instead proceeded to call the vote?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: We were expecting the Governor and we had made a reservation for where he was to sit in line with the Standing Orders. However, when he sent the lawyers, they requested to watch brief and they were given a designated place to watch brief for the suspended Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Therefore, to that question, your answer is that the Assembly did not hear the Governor's lawyers at all?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The Assembly was technically constrained by the Standing Orders to admit lawyers in the plenary.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Whether because of the Standing Orders or otherwise, they were not heard at all. They were told go to the gallery and watch like everybody else.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: In line with the Standing Orders, we had designated a place for the Governor on the right hand of the Speaker but he failed to appear.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: That is okay. We know you are evading the question but it is a question of fact. It is good that you have acknowledged that the Speaker acknowledged that two counsel had been sent to represent the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: To watch brief.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Whatever you want to call it. They were there as the Governor's representatives. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I may need your direction on this. In the course of the cross- examination, there has been an admission that part of the documents that are being relied upon by the County Assembly were actually not documents that were available to the Governor or in the proceedings before the County Assembly. Rule 19 of the 5th Schedule of the Standing Orders expressly states that no additional documents should be adduced by the County Assembly. The directions we seek is that no further reference should be made to those additional documents because they are highly prejudicial to the Governor's case.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. The counsel was cross-examining and once he is done, we will need to have an opportunity for re- examination. If he then wants to address the question of admissibility of documents, he needs to make an application which we can respond to. However, he cannot do that in the course of the cross-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Charles Njenga
entries.text: Very well. We shall reserve our application for further time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Standing Orders do allow very limited re-examination for clarification. I just have three questions for clarification. Mr. Solomon, you were asked by the first counsel whether you had received the notice of preliminary objection. The question I want to ask you is, did you receive the notice of preliminary objection before or after the County Assembly had filed its record?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: After the filing.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Therefore, by the time the County Assembly was filing its evidence as required by the rules and the Standing Orders, you were not aware that the question of quorum as is alleged was going to be raised?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: I only became aware after receiving preliminary objection.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: You were asked a question around appointments and not given an opportunity to respond. I would like you to look at page 123. Can you tell us what that is and if you can read the first paragraph of that memo? Who is it from?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It is coming from the County Secretary and the Head of Public Service.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: What does it say?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: It goes to the Director of Human Resource Management.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Just read the paragraph.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The stoppage of salaries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Read the first paragraph there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: The following officers were appointed by His Excellency Governor and issued with appointment letters signed by him contrary to the laid down procedures. In view of this, therefore, urgently stop any further payments of salaries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Therefore, there is evidence that one of the required officers actually identified that breach.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: You were also asked about conflict of interest and whether you are aware of criminal cases against the Governor. Are you aware of any criminal case against the Governor that that touches on allegations of conflict of interest that you have raised in these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, counsel. I am aware of one case where he is charged jointly with Susan Wangari Ndung'u.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Is it in respect of the charges here or is it a separate matter?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: That is a separate matter relating to a special purpose vehicle formed for the purposes of benefitting from Kshs588 million road tenders.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: That is not what you have took before the County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: That is separate. It is not related with any of this.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: In paragraph 29 in your witness statement, you have referred to various people as relatives of Hon. Waititu, the wife and the daughters. Do you personally know Governor Waititu's wives?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, I personally know both Susan Wangari Ndung'u, who occupies the Office of the First Lady Kiambu and Esther Wamuyu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I have an objection because this is re-examination. I did not ask this witness whether he has personal knowledge of those persons. I asked of evidence, documentary evidence, so that my learned friend will be extending the purview of that question; reopening that question or revisiting areas I did not touch. If I had posed the question whether he has personal knowledge, then it would be in order for my learned senior to re-examine this witness on that question. This will be reopening that question and I was very specific, and I limited the scope of my question in cross-examination. This is the re-examine if I understand it, is on clarification on an issue that arose. Therefore, it has to be pegged on the question that I asked. As to personal knowledge, if - and the HANSARD can bear me out - if I raised a question regarding his personal knowledge or otherwise, then it will be open for my learned senior, with due respect, to re-examine this witness on that question. I invite you to give directions on that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: My learned friend's objection is based on a false premise. The premise that he brought and he was trying to be a little too clever with the witness is to say that evidence is documents; that is not true. Evidence is not documents. Personal testimony is also evidence. Therefore, he asked him whether he has any evidence that this lady is the wife of the Governor, then he quickly followed it up to say do you have documentary evidence. You have brought the question of whether there is evidence that Susan Wangari Ndung'u is a wife of Ferdinand Waititu. That is the question that he has a right to respond to. When he told you, he was there for the Ngurario, you quickly ran away from the question.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Laughter)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Okay, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Just one last question, you were referred to Rule No.19 of the Fifth Schedule which are the rules of procedure of this House and you were asked whether you have introduced any new evidence that was not a part of the allegations. So, the question that I want to ask you, Solomon, is this; all the documents that were identified and which you confirmed were additional evidence, were they evidence of additional allegations or did they relate to the allegations that you had dealt with?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Not at all. They all relate to the allegations that were presented on the Floor of the County Assembly on the 3rd December, 2019.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: In respect of the allegations on the land, is there a witness who is coming to testify on that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Solomon Kinuthia Wambui
entries.text: Yes, there is.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: I have no further re-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Next witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: The next witness is Mr. Erick Kiriko.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Manage your time, because you have two hours to go.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we were directed that the witnesses would be in a holding room, and we had asked that they be called as we are approaching.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The witness for Kiambu County Assembly, Mr. Erick Kiriko, took the oath)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Kiriko, please, give the House your full names, your profession and tell us what you do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am Erick Kelvin Kiriko. I work for the County Government of Kiambu as the Legal Advisor to the Acting Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: What is your training, Mr. Kiriko?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I am a lawyer. I have an LLB from the University of Hull in the United Kingdom (UK), and also a master's degree from the same university.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Have you provided a witness statement in these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes, I have, and it is particularised and paginated as No.1 in the bundle of documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: I think each witness statement starts at page one, so it is the third witness statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes. I am sorry; I was referring to my letter which I had written to the Commission on Administration of Justice (CAJ); that was No.1.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Mr. Kiriko, can you tell us the gist of your testimony; what it is that you have put in your witness statement?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Essentially, I wrote to the CAJ and I had asked for further particulars on certain information which was in the public realm. I wrote a letter dated 30th October, 2019, and got a response dated 19th November, 2019, from the CAJ. I was asking for information in respect to some property. This was part of a press release by the Chairlady of the CAJ. It essentially alluded to some property in Thika which had been transferred to one Esther Wamuyu Nyatu. The essence of the report was that this property had been transferred improperly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: What documents did you receive from the CAJ?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I received a bundle of documents. It is from page 58, which was in response to my letter. There was a bundle of documents which, amongst other things, included the press statement which had been released and which I alluded to on the 26th. It also contained a certificate of lease. It also contained documentation which showed the property had been transferred to one Esther Wamuyu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: In the report that you received from CAJ - and I want to refer you to page 70, because we do not need to go through all of it - can you tell us what the Commission's conclusions and recommendations were, as contained in that Report?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Actually, the findings and conclusions are on page 57, No. 3, where they said that the recommendations of the office was that---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Let us start with the conclusions, and then come to the recommendations.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Okay. Basically in the conclusion, if I may read out, it says:- "That the investigations looked into the alleged irregular transfer of ownership of the plots and abuse of power by officers involved in the transfer process. Based on the foregoing, the investigation confirmed that the two plots - and they are referred to there - belonged to Mrs. Cecilia Njoki Mbugua, and that they were irregularly transferred to Ms. Esther Nyatu Wamuyu." It then concludes that, "The plots have since been reverted to the rightful owner, a Mrs. Cecilia Mbugua." That was the conclusion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: What were the recommendations of the Commission?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: The Commission said that the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) should institute prosecution against Ferdinard Waititu; the Governor of Kiambu County, for abuse of power and fraud; and that the County Government of Kiambu should expedite the long overdue approval of the development plans to enable Mrs. Mbugua to embark on her projects. The Commission also called upon the land registrars to exercise due diligence while conducting land transfers, including inviting all interested parties for consent.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: If you look at page 54, which is really just a reproduction of Article 59(4), can you confirm what the mandate of the CAJ is, as relates to the charge that had been levelled?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: It says that the Commission has been mandated under Article 59(4)(2) H and J of our Constitution and the Commission of Administration of Justice Act, 2011, to inter alia investigate any conduct in state affairs or any act or omission in public administration in any sphere of Government and complaints of abuse of office, unfair treatment or manifest injustice of unlawful, oppressive, unfair or unresponsive official conduct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: You are familiar with the Constitution; you told us you are a lawyer?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: Do you know the provisions of Article 39 with the right to correction of errors in reports?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes. I am particularly aware also of Article 40, which also talks about someone enjoying the right of their property. I will have to refer to 39.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: So, to your knowledge, when did you say that you learnt about the press statement by the CAJ?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: It was about the end of September. It was widely circulated. It was in the press; both print and broadcast. I actually got it on the news and the newspapers the day after.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: To your knowledge, do you know whether Gov. Waititu ever made a petition to have any of the findings of the CAJ deleted, revoked, or in any way retracted?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I am not aware of that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Njoroge Nani Mungai
entries.text: You are not aware. Thank you. Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is all for this witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, and hon. Senators. I just have a few questions in close examination, then I leave the Floor to my learned colleagues. Mr. Kiriko, just confirm that you assumed the position of legal advisor on 27th August 2019 after the Governor had already been barred from accessing office owing to the charges that he is currently facing?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes, I confirm that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, when the matters that you have alluded to took place, you were actually not serving in the stated capacity. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: What happened? Please, repeat.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: The matters that are the subject of this report by the Ombudsman. They were matters that took place prior to your assumption of office as the legal advisor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes. If you look at the press statement, we started on the investigations on 5th March 2019. At that time, I was not in that capacity.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: That is fine. You have made reference at paragraph 4 of the charges that you became aware of. It says "that I became aware of the charges leveled against the Governor of Kiambu County sometimes on the 22nd September 2019." Which charges are you referring to? Are they the charges before this Senate which are the subject of this impeachment?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: No, they are not these charges.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Which charges are you referring to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I was actually referring to the press statement which was released by the Ombudsman.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, the press statement is a charge. That was a charge against the honourable governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: It was not a charge, but they made recommendations.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Okay. You said that "I am aware the complaint with respect to the properties belonging to Cecilia Njoki Mbugua is one of the charges. First and foremost, Mr. Kiriko, because it appears you have some keen interest in this particular transaction. I am sure that, perhaps as part of your investigation, you may have taken a statement from the victim of this alleged fraud who is Cecilia Njoki. Did you get a statement from her? You seem to be the one investigating this matter. That is why you even wrote to the Ombudsman. Did you take a statement from this lady who is the alleged victim of this fraud?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I did not take a statement from her.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But you appreciate that she is a victim of the fraud and not the Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You confirm that she has not filed a statement. There is actually no statement from the victim of this fraud before the Senate to say this is what the Governor did or did not do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I think if you look at the letter that was written to me by the Ombudsman---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is on which page?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Give me a second.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Which page?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: There is an affidavit which is there. This is not my bundle. I think I can have it if I have my bundle. I have seen it. If you look at page 98, you will find an affidavit from the lady Cecilia Njoki Mbugua. This was part of the documents which were sent to me by the Ombudsman.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: If you look at this affidavit. It is a very short affidavit. She is saying that she is a legal and bona fide owner of that piece of land. She is still in possession of that land. She has not sold that land to anybody. She has conducted a search and was surprised to find some name. Though I signed the transfer documents, I signed them under duress from officials of the County Government of Kiambu. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: And paying rates ex cetera . In that particular affidavit which is allegedly signed by Cecilia Njoki Mbugua, does it say who these officials or officers are? Does it say that the Governor unduly influenced her to sign a transfer of her property from this affidavit?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: It does not say that specifically.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: But if my learned---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It is okay. You will have a chance to be reexamined by your counsel. I am just interested in the content of that. You have confirmed that Cecilia Njoki Mbugua is not one of the witnesses who have been lined up to appear and testify before this Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: It was opened to the Assembly given that this is a very critical charge to get this lady to come and testify before this Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: And that the Assembly, in fact, did not find it necessary to get this lady to come and testify before this Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I believe you can ask that question to the Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But she is not one of the witnesses lined up.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you. Let us move on. You realise, Mr. Kiriko, as a lawyer, that this is a case of alleged fraud.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Are you aware of any investigations by DCI on account of these facts?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: In respect to this issue of the Ombudsman?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: In respect of this issue of a lady who was allegedly defrauded of her property by the Governor. Are you aware of any investigations in that respect?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I am aware of recommendations for investigations, but I am not aware of any investigations.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, your answer is that you are not aware that there has been any investigations by DCI on account of this complaint? Are you aware whether, perhaps, the Governor is facing charges again on account of this alleged fraud in any court in this country?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I am aware that he has been charged.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: No, on account of fraud or defrauding this lady called Cecilia Njoki Mbugua.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I repeat what I said. I am aware that there are recommendations.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You appreciate, as a lawyer, there is a difference between recommendation and actual charge.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, my question is whether you are aware if the Governor has been charged in any court of law on account of this alleged fraud.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I am not aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Thank you very much. You said that you wrote a letter to CAJ on 30th October 2019. What may have prompted you to write this letter -you as Kiriko - the legal advisor to the Deputy Governor? What may have prompted you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: When I heard about it, I did not have all the particulars. So, I thought I could get better information from the body which reported it and investigated it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: What was the motivation? You appreciate that you are not an investigator, are you?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: That is why I asked the right body to give information.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: The question is what could have motivated you? Obviously, you cannot just wake up one morning and decide to write to the Office of the Ombudsman, not on any other matter, but on a matter touching the Governor. What could have been the motivation, if any?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I think I will be a dereliction of my duties if I did not ask for any information on something which was pertinent to our county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Is that part of your job description as the legal advisor to the Deputy Governor to write letters touching on alleged private matters between persons? Is it part of your job description?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: First of all, I think I will answer that question by saying it is not a private matter. It is a matter which pertains to governance. This was the Governor of the County.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: But you appreciate the question I posed and you seem to be prevaricating on that question. What was the motivation? Why this particular matter touching on the Governor and not any other matter being dealt with by the Office of the Ombudsman?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: If you look at my letter which I wrote, I referred to myself as a voter of Kiambu.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Where is that letter? On what page, kindly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Just go to page one.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Are you referring to Page one of the document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, you are saying that you submitted this request in the spirit secured in the Constitution in respect of public access of information. So, what do you want to do with that information?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is important to know what the Governor is doing because I am a voter in that county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: So, in all matters that the governor does, you write letters to the Ombudsman to inquire about them?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: No, they gave information in respect to this matter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: Let us move on. You have substantially referred to this report. First and foremost, when you requested for it, I presume that the Office of the Ombudsman does some investigation before writing a report. They write to persons of interest asking for statements and comments in furtherance of their rights to be heard. Were you served with the official transcript of the proceedings that took place before the Office of the Ombudsman in which the Governor is said to have admitted the matter forms the basis or content of the report of the ombudsman? Do you have any official transcript from the Office of the Ombudsman that state the day they conducted the proceedings, the Governor appeared in person and what is stated? Just like the way the court transcript is recorded, did you get it so that we can see what exactly the Governor is said to have said with respect to these matters?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: There is no transcript but they allege to what he had said.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: You appreciate that the transcript is what would tell us what exactly the Governor admitted to? There must have been some recorded proceedings? This is an investigative office which investigates complaints. So, you appreciate that the transcript would be there but you did not ask for it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I did not ask for it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: In fact, from the documents that you have produced, do you have a statement in the hand of the Governor admitting to this alleged fraud with respect to the land that belonged to the widow?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: I do not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: In essence, you are telling the Senate that the only evidence you have of this alleged commission of a crime under national law which you have fashioned as fraud is just a report from the Office of the Ombudsman, there is no transcript, evidence or admissions in the hand of the Governor. Is that your evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: The evidence is what I have attached here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: If you look at those leases and transfers, can you point out to a transfer from the name of this lady, Cecilia Njoki Mbugua, to one Ferdinand Ndung'u Waititu babayao?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: There is none.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: There is no single document other than reference to the report of the Ombudsman that shows that the Governor obtained any interest over land or those properties that you have referred to.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ng'ang'a Mbugua
entries.text: I yield the Floor to my learned colleagues to ask a few questions to this witness. Lastly, Mr. Kiriko, could you kindly confirm that you were employed by the Deputy Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes, I confirm.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Mbuthi Gathenji
entries.text: That is all for this witness. Do you wish to produce your witness statement as evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Erick Kiriko
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Mbuthi Gathenji
entries.text: We have realised that the testimony of the other witness that we were supposed to call, Mr. Edwin Njuguna, was adequately covered by Hon. Solomon. We will, therefore, not call any further witnesses and that in terms of evidence, that is the close of the County Assembly's case.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Hon. Senators, it is time for requests or clarifications. You have two minutes. Kindly, say whom you are addressing the question to. This is now open for Senators.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Murkomen?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, to the best of my knowledge, the witnesses are not here although the first witness is. Is it in order for you to call the witness who has just finished so that we can ask those clarifications?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let the witness come back.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am curious whether we are only restricted to seeking clarification from the witness or we can look at the entire submissions including the opening statements made by the Governor because it forms part of the submissions and argument. That is what I want clarification on, if we are only restricted to seeking clarification from the witnesses, it is good to bring the witnesses back.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, therefore, a direction should be given that the County Assembly has not closed their case. If they have closed their case, we are reopening it. The rules will be that if Senators ask a question which needs clarification, every question that is asked, after it is completed, lawyers must re-examine it with their witnesses. Therefore, it is important to make that clear.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Speaker consulted with the Clerk-at-the-Table)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I need your ear and eye. Can I proceed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Yes, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mutula Kilonzo Jnr
entries.text: .: That direction on how the questions will be asked and whether all of them will be asked and then re-examination is done on either side is important so that we know how to proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Rule No.22 states that:- "A Senator may, in not more than two minutes or such further time as the Speaker may determine put a question to any of the witnesses, a party or the counsel representing a party.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that rule is applicable in the course of proceedings. When a witness is still on oath and on the stand, any Senator who had any issue to clarify would have been entitled to do that. The relevant counsel would re- examine the witness before we step him down. We have already heard the two witnesses and the case is closed. We cannot start to reopen the case unless we reopen the hearing again to the extent that if any witness is called back for any Senator to ask a question, each of the two lawyers plus the Governor would be entitled to ask questions again. That does not look neat at all and it is not procedural. If we find that this is not way to go, I ask that you move us to the next level.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: There is provision for that already so you do not have to ask. Kindly, proceed, Sen. Murkomen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are going to re-open a Pandora's Box if we go that way. It will be a circus by itself. If we call the witnesses back on the stand, the Members will ask questions and we will wonder whether the lawyers of both sides will have a right to ask the same questions. We will go round in circles. If the House is in agreement, we should let the matter lie there but in the next stage, if one needs clarification, it should come at the stage where the examination has been done and cross-examination is being done. You can give us a chance to seek clarifications before you stand the witness down so that in re-examination, the lawyer of the County Assembly in this sense will have had the opportunity to respond.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Hon. Senators, as I had mentioned, all that is in our Standing Orders but you do not have to ask. Reading the mood of the House, we will not ask for clarifications at this point in time.

entries.label: heading
entries.text: ADJOURNMENT

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text:
The House now stands adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00 am

The Senate rose at 4.25 p.m.
